tasks.title: Carry the target binding through local operation seams
tasks.goal: Carry an opt-in target binding through strict local operation records and refuse bound effects until the physical owner grants pinned roots.
steps: Trace existing deploy/native and extension request carriers, add an optional typed binding without changing legacy local operation meaning or serialized None bytes.

Use host-issued context/target binding values from M-16 conventions; keep a distinct bound state key, include binding in bound plan hash, and validate intent, receipt, native request and structured inspection equality before replay.

Refuse bound apply before inverse recovery, provider selection or state creation when no pinned host root/effect grant exists; never derive one from a request body or package descriptor. C.2 supplies the first supported bound effect.
positive_cases: The same package under two injected instance bindings gets distinct state keys and typed receipt/inspection identities without touching either destination.
A legacy local compatibility request keeps the incumbent projected files and byte-compatible unbound records.
negative_cases: A request body path or package descriptor self-grants a new root.
A copied legacy or other-instance receipt is accepted under a bound key, or unsupported bound apply reaches recovery/provider.

acceptance: Target binding survives the typed request/plan/journal/receipt/inspection carrier and legacy None remains byte-compatible.
Bound effects without admitted physical roots refuse before recovery/provider; no successful native or builtin effect is claimed by C.1.
tasks.safe_stop: Bound carrier and early-refusal tests pass; first real bound effect and physical alias fencing remain C.2.

notes: Planned permanent destination: vibevm/vibespecs/common/PROP-076-environment-model.xml; forward metadata only until the promotion leaf creates the governing anchor.

Bind the smallest affected target and exact cases before compiling. Discover from source/metadata, then list only the bound target/case and require a nonzero match. Add broader checks only for demonstrated affected behavior that the selected checks cannot establish.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.

The expanded schema/wire/CLI/orchestrator perimeter is limited to the opt-in target-binding carrier and its mechanically required codegen/constructor/validation changes. M-14-C.2 owns physical alias/root-handle fencing.

The incumbent builtin vibe-bin provider writes through raw paths; C.1 must not enable bound effects merely by pinning an unrelated Project handle. C.2 owns handle-constrained I/O and shared physical locking before the first bound UserProfile apply.

tasks.title: Fence aliased roots and stale target generations
tasks.goal: Fence aliased roots and stale target generations, then admit the first supported local bound builtin effect through pinned root handles.
steps: Extend the existing physical resource identity/lease boundary to recognize equivalent roots across environment instances.
Revalidate root handle, principal, generation and resource ownership at admission and commit; keep logical config-member ownership under a shared physical file lock.
Add temporary-root concurrency/replay tests covering alias roots, relocated directories and third-state changes; record exact partial truth if drift occurs after a landed write.

Move the first successful bound local UserProfile vibe-bin apply behind pinned host root handles and a shared physical destination lock; provider I/O must use the admitted handles or an equivalent verified capability path, never only checked strings.

Carry optional binding through pending/committed lock sidecar, checkpoint and inverse markers as well as intent/receipt; absent legacy binding retains exact old bytes. Bound interrupted intent or missing sidecar never uses legacy reconstruction and keeps a recovery-required/partial result after possible publication.
positive_cases: Disjoint injected homes can proceed independently.
Two aliases of one root conflict even when their logical instance IDs differ.
The same package bytes deployed into two disjoint injected homes create distinct physical outputs and bound receipts under their admitted principals.
negative_cases: Expired generation or changed root reuses an earlier plan.
Equal file bytes transfer ownership between receipt families.
A changed request body root, unsupported target mode/OS or provider scope escalation reaches a bound provider effect after a host grant was minted.
A copied bound sidecar, checkpoint or inverse from another instance/principal is accepted through legacy fallback during recovery.
